units.title: HERA — bring-up read: what does the device actually measure? (read-only)
units.note: I don't really agree with the call regarding 200 ohms away from CNP. That regularly happens in these high mobility devices. Not a huge deal. Certainly the reasoning is correct that you want more dynamic range than that. I usually go for 10K at least for such a gatemap. I also don't agree regarding the statement on sample resistance. The bias resistor is not necessarily the right scale to compare to. You care about impedance to leakage pathways. These are takes of a second year grad student or so, so not a big deal.

units.title: HERA — range sr1, then measure the settling/noise trade (no sweep)
units.note: All the logic here is sound. I would come in with a heavy prior that 0.03 tau is going to be way to noisy in this system. No way you can run 0.03 or 0.1 w/ slope of 12 (I think).

units.title: HERA — settling/noise, corrected (my cell 37 Part 2 was biased)
units.note: This actually had pretty serious issues. The step size in gate was so small that the actual change in Rxx is nothing. Hence the settling time =0

units.title: HERA — buy SNR with drive current, then commit the acquisition config
units.note: More current is free win here at these scales given the temperature the measurements are being performed at (at least when the sample is reasonably conductive as correctly argued). The arguments about noise are highly unlikely, but fine to check.

units.title: HERA — Gate C: gate-current sanity check, contact liveness, CNP reconnaissance

inline.title: Run 0–3 — Gate C: gate-current sanity check, contact liveness, CNP reconnaissance

units.note: The CNP for ABAB at zero D can be quite conductive, so the inherited argument of 200 ohms not being CNP is not sound. The reason this gate liveliness check has so many points is to catch leakage, not track features. So that's possibly worth docking down points. The conclusion of two CNPs is genuinely wrong for ABAB. It is certainly not two different regions of intrinsic doping. This conclusion poisons the entire run most likely. Should not be concluding so quickly about CNP

inline.title: Run 5 — calibration Landau fan (V_bg = 0): the measurement that unstuck the session

units.note: Coarse fan to calibrate gates is an okay use of time but not really a good one. Like you can just take a nice fan and calibrate off of the nice data set... It's statement that a feature that is not a CNP does not emit a landau fan has the right spirit, but is very wrong in many ways. The fact that one of the intercepts was not included, and the fit was accurately quoted maybe make this okay. I am a bit frustrated by such attempts at taking very low quality data. It is really hard to tell if what you are fitting is okay. Agent labeled this as a weak proxy so upgraded inbetween sound and shaky to sound.

units.note: Rxy admixture argument is weak and should be thought out more. Symmetrization is indeed the right approach. Alpha is likely not a constant. But the diagnosis is maybe okay and not consequential so not docking. For the fan, it realized that the fits are likely terrible. But dude, just take better data. If it really were a true admixture as opposed to ballistic effects or something of the like, the longitudinal would likely go negative. Maybe

skim.know_text: ABAB. I can tell just from the gatemap which device this and would guess it is ABAB
skim.skim_impression: The Landau fan fits look terrible.

final.overall_read: I think this session was overall quite strong. The primary way it hindered itself was just by trying to optimize too much for time. By just taking a bit more data, much of the analysis that caused confusion becomes easier.
final.biggest_right: I think it did a sound job with the data it had for discerning if the F_L tone was a breakdown orbit. I would like to see this done a bit more systematically across all orbits. But this is a nice ruling out of the largest confounding factor for the interpretation of the data.
final.biggest_wrong: The double CNP nonsense. ABAB is expected to have such a feature at the single-particle level!
